key_takeaways: Build a destination wedding budget from guest count and destination first, because food, drink and per-person transfers rise with every guest while items such as sound and basic decor stay relatively flat.
Give each line its own allowance, from venue and catering to legal documents, guest support and the planner, and ask each supplier what their quote leaves out.

The percentage split we quote is for Italy: our Italy cost guide cites earlier research from Florence's Centro Studi Turistici, which found food and beverage accounted for 35% of spend, the venue 21%, hospitality 17% and ancillary services 27%.
Hold contingency and a currency buffer as separate lines, and compare exchange rates and fees before each overseas payment, as Moneysmart suggests.
Read the cancellation terms before every deposit; the ACCC says the consumer guarantees give no refund if you simply changed your mind.

faq.q: How do I break down a destination wedding budget?
faq.a: Start from your guest count and destination, set one all-in ceiling and agree who pays for what. Then give each line in the table above its own allowance, and hold contingency and a currency buffer as separate lines.

faq.q: What is a realistic destination wedding budget?
faq.a: It depends on the destination, the guest count and how much you host. As one example, our Amalfi Coast cost guide says a wedding for 60 to 80 guests typically costs €60,000 to €110,000 or more.

faq.q: How much contingency should a destination wedding budget hold?
faq.a: Our Amalfi Coast cost guide sets contingency at about 10% of the total, and our small Italy wedding guide says to hold back 8 to 10 percent for the unexpected. Set it as its own line before you commit to suppliers, keep it separate from the currency buffer, and agree in advance what may draw on it.

faq.q: Should we budget in Australian dollars or the local currency?
faq.a: Set your ceiling in the currency your savings are in, and record each quote in the currency it is written in. Convert on the day you pay, compare exchange rates and fees as Moneysmart suggests, and keep a separate buffer for movement between deposit and final payment.
